briefs.source_chain: German state elections deal further blows to the CDU (record AfD result in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Die Linke topping Berlin, CDU missing the 5% threshold in one state for the first time since WWII) therefore Germany's political centre weakens without an immediate national policy shift; separately a US-Denmark-Greenland deal reduces Greenland-related geopolitical risk versus Trump's earlier ambitions; Asian equities rally on trade-talk optimism ahead of the Trump-Xi summit; the week ahead (flash PMIs, Norges/Riksbank/SNB decisions, heavy Fed speak, payrolls) plays out against a hawkish post-hike Fed backdrop; last week's initial stagflation-driven spike above a 5% 10yr yield was reversed mainly by falling oil (not the Fed hike), while French spreads over bunds widened past 100bp for the first time since 2012.
briefs.brief_chain: Same causal chain: CDU losses weaken Germany's centre without a national policy shift; the Greenland deal lowers event risk; Asian markets rally on trade optimism into the Trump-Xi summit; the week's calendar unfolds under a hawkish Fed; last week's yield spike above 5% was unwound by falling oil more than by the Fed hike, with French-bund spreads breaking 100bp for the first time since 2012.

briefs.source_chain: The September FOMC hiked 25bp unanimously to 3.75-4% and shifted its inflation language to flag broad-based (not just energy-driven) price pressure, therefore the SEP showed higher growth, lower unemployment, higher core PCE, and a Committee seeing only upside inflation risk and no downside employment risk, therefore SG reads the Committee as prioritizing inflation over stagflation risk, therefore SG keeps its call for two more 25bp hikes (December, March) to 75bp total, conditional on inflation data not disappointing.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain: hawkish hike and statement shift signal broadening inflation concern; SEP revisions (growth up, unemployment to 4.1% vs 4.2% long-run, core PCE to 3.4%) and the upside-inflation/no-downside-employment risk skew read as lower stagflation risk and inflation-focused policy; 2026 dot implies 50bp more this year (12/19 aligned), 2027 dots split 4 cutters vs 8 hikers, long-run dot to 3.2%; Warsh frames the hike as removing accommodation from a not-restrictive stance; SG keeps two more 25bp hikes (Dec, March, 75bp total) toward unwinding the 2025 insurance cuts, conditional on inflation cooperating.

distortions.what: Brief states Warsh 'called current policy not restrictive.' The source sentence describing this is garbled/self-contradictory ('didn't view the current Fed's policy stance has been not restrictive'), but the attached quote ('removing a dose of accommodation') and corroborating same-day source notes (MS: 'has not yet reached clearly restrictive territory'; GS: Sehgal reading 'removing a dose of accommodation' as more hikes ahead) confirm the brief's reading is the intended one.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — this resolves a garbled OCR sentence to its evident intended meaning, corroborated elsewhere; no stance, hike call, or invalidation condition depends on the wording.

briefs.source_chain: MS shifts its US baseline from benign Middle East de-escalation to an oil risk-premium scenario as converging supply-chain disruptions erode the buffers that previously absorbed oil shocks, therefore oil stays elevated (WTI $107.02, Brent $130.80) and the SPR falls to its lowest since April 1984, therefore second-round inflation effects delay assumed airfare disinflation and core PCE is revised up (3.2% 2026, 2.7% 2027), therefore 2027 growth/consumption/investment are trimmed and unemployment is raised, therefore MS now expects two more 25bp hikes (December, March) to a 4.25-4.50% terminal rate — a baseline MS assigns 45% probability.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain, same figures and same 45% baseline probability (confirmed against Exhibit 31: 'Baseline: Oil Risk Premium/Sticky Inflation (45%)').

briefs.source_chain: GS's floor note aggregates GCEM symposium soundbites: Fed speakers frame the hike as the Committee still viewing policy as accommodative after years of inflation misses, with ~100bp of cumulative hikes now priced, while rates strategists argue Fed credibility has removed a source of long-end instability even as AI-driven issuance and fiscal deficits add term-premium pressure; on oil, Struyven says Mideast supply (near pre-war levels) and China demand weakness 'remain intact' for now, capping prices below a $125+ tail, while every 10% sustained cut to Mideast exports would add ~$20/bbl and Cohen warns markets underprice the risk of that China demand 'shock absorber' being removed; a parallel gas-price scenario could force ECB/CEEMEA hikes; therefore, since clients are broadly long EM carry/frontier FX/equities-tech/received EM rates, GS recommends four hedges (SPX lookback puts, USD binary calls vs CHF/EUR, QQQ dual/tri-binaries, outright Brent calls) against an oil-driven yields-up/equities-down shock.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain and same four trades, except it states 'China's demand offset is fading' rather than the source's 'remains intact for now, with the risk it could be removed.'

distortions.what: Brief asserts 'China's demand offset is fading,' but the source (Struyven) explicitly says Mideast supply and China demand weakness 'remain intact' for now as the forces capping oil's upside — the removal of that offset is a hypothetical risk Cohen flags ('remove that shock absorber'), not a stated present trend.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — GS's four hedges are offered as insurance against the oil-spike tail scenario regardless of whether the China demand offset is currently intact or already eroding; no trade, instrument, or conviction level changes.
